1.pericope_label: In the ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the tenth month, came Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon and all his army against Jerusalem
debates: Whether six princes are named or three with their titles
Why the opening verses stand here at all
outliers: Clarke reduces the six names to three and suspects a copying error in the first of them
Calvin declines the whole question of the names as doubtful and of no great moment
themes: A prophet turning historian to seal his own words
A city that bore eighteen months of famine
Strength gone the way of a shorn Samson
A forum taken as an encampment

4.pericope_label: when Zedekiah the king of Judah saw them, and all the men of war, then they fled, and went forth out of the city by night
debates: How the king got out of a besieged city
Where he was trying to go
Why Riblah was the place of judgment
Why he was blinded rather than killed
outliers: Clarke has the king making for Egypt across the Jordan, where Ellicott has him making for the open country of Gilead
Calvin reads the sparing of the king life as a way of killing him a hundred times over
themes: A tower used to watch an enemy arrive
A road chosen because it was quicker
A plain empty enough to hide a king
Two prophecies fulfilled by one cruelty

8.pericope_label: And the Chaldeans burned the king’s house, and the houses of the people, with fire, and brake down the walls of Jerusalem
debates: What the title of the captain of the guard means
Why the deserters were carried off along with the defenders
Why the poorest of the people were left in the land
outliers: Calvin suggests the deserters may themselves have asked to be taken, since they would not have been safe at home once the army withdrew
Calvin reads the leaving of the poor as evidence that God shows care by keeping men low
themes: A singular house standing for every house
An officer whose title means chief of the slayers
Land given away to secure a tribute
Beggars left owning the fields of nobles

11.pericope_label: Now Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon gave charge concerning Jeremiah to Nebuzar–adan the captain of the guard
debates: How the king of Babylon came to know of Jeremiah
What looking well to him required
Why Gedaliah was chosen as his keeper
Whether he was released at the prison or at Ramah
outliers: Calvin illustrates the danger to the prophet from the death of Archimedes at the storming of Syracuse, killed by a common soldier despite orders to spare him
Henry reads the order as a reproach, since the prophet found better usage from a heathen king than from his own princes
themes: Mercy sung after a chapter of judgment
A great soul noticing the meanest sufferer
A pagan king serving a purpose he never intended
Three generations of one house friendly to prophets

15.pericope_label: Now the word of the Lord came unto Jeremiah, while he was shut up in the court of the prison
debates: Why an earlier word is placed at the end of the chapter
Why the promise is grounded on trust rather than on the kindness shown
What a life given for a prey means
outliers: Calvin hears in the promise to a foreigner an indirect reproof of the children of Abraham after the flesh
Ellicott argues that the prophet would not have recorded the prediction unless he already knew it had come true
themes: A prophet who cannot leave his prison to deliver a message
One man standing out when others were silenced by fear
A promise given early so that its hearer would not run
Bare life counted as spoil after a shipwreck
